title: Help without a claim of ownership

captions.physics: Considering the actual amount of help
captions.energy: Seeking to overcome a shared obstacle
captions.emotions: Feeling attachment and an unspoken debt

meaning: Your active support remains considerate when an honest measure of help does not become a right to hold on to each other.
text: A warm impulse to help can sit beside a wish to become indispensable. In the physical position of Anahata, Justice draws attention to an honest measure of involvement and the consequences of agreements. The Chariot in energy brings a wish to overcome an obstacle and achieve movement where doing things alone is difficult. The Devil in emotions describes attachment in which support can feel like debt or a way of securing closeness. You may accomplish a great deal together, but each person’s freedom after accepting help matters especially.

For example, you assemble a large shelving unit together. One offers to finish it despite initially promising only an hour. You clarify whether continuing is manageable and what each person expects. **A contribution does not buy authority over another person.** The completed shelf can please both of you when it conceals no later bill for time, attention or compulsory agreement with every subsequent plan.

Difficulty arises when the amount of help becomes a measure of entitlement to someone. The more effort you make, the harder it feels to let the other person decline a request in return. Care then binds even within an apparently fair exchange. Closeness benefits from naming expectations before further effort and recognising that gratitude does not mean endless availability. Support need not make anyone indispensable.
